## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Ambajātaka* (Ja 474) is a birth story in the Pali Jātaka collection [SuttaCentral]. According to the frame narrative set at Jetavana, the Buddha told this story concerning Devadatta, who had repudiated his teacher, caused a schism in the Saṅgha, and subsequently fell into the Avīci hell [SuttaCentral]. In the conclusion (*samodhāna*) of the past story, the Buddha connects the narrative to the present, explaining that Devadatta had likewise repudiated his teacher in a past life and met with great ruin as an ungrateful pupil (*akataññū māṇavo*), while Ānanda was the king and the Bodhisatta was a *caṇḍālaputta* [Fausböll 1887].

Verses from the *Ambajātaka* are included in canonical selections of Buddhist wisdom verses [Anandajoti 2010]. In terms of text reuse, DharmaNexus identifies 18 matching segments between the verses of Ja 474 and the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (fourth volume, Atk S0513a4), with the longest shared passage spanning §2.1–4.4 against commentary segments §1851–1860 [DharmaNexus]. Neither SuttaCentral nor DharmaNexus records any cross-language parallels or alignments in Sanskrit, Chinese, or Tibetan [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].
